title: The Weaver's Last Thread
story:
James stood at the edge of the Plaza of the Fountain, watching droplets of highland rain catch the afternoon sunlight as they cascaded down the tiered stone basin. He reached out a small, cautious hand to touch the damp stone, feeling the cool moisture that reminded him of the misty mornings in the Great Canopy. The plaza stretched out before him in a wide expanse of glistening cobblestones, framed by shuttered merchant windows and the soft hum of Oakhaven settling into evening.

Seeking a moment of quiet away from the returning crowds, James ducked beneath a low stone archway that led off the main plaza into a narrower, quieter lane. He had not gone more than a few paces before a familiar, rhythmic wooden clatter reached his ears, echoing gently off the damp brick walls. Drawn by the comforting sound, he followed the passage until he found himself peering into the open doorway of a small, sunlit workshop.

Inside, Mateo sat patiently before his traditional wooden loom, his hands moving with practiced grace as he shuttled a fresh shuttle of indigo thread through the warp. Without looking up, the weaver smiled and greeted James as if he had only stepped out for a brief errand, bridging the days since their last meeting with a quiet, welcoming warmth. Mateo gestured toward a small wooden stool near the hearth, offering James a dry place to rest his feet and watch the shuttle dance across the frame.

As the light outside began to fade into a deep amber twilight, James sat cross-legged on the floor, fingering the colorful threads braided around his leather strap and feeling the gentle hum of the loom vibrate through the floorboards. The world outside Oakhaven was vast and filled with distant horizons, but here in the quiet warmth of the workshop, the town felt wonderfully small and safe. He closed his eyes for a moment, listening to the steady rhythm of the loom, and whispered his habitual greeting to the coming night.
